newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM urges king not to abdicate.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM urges king not to abdicate.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Monday urged his father, King Norodom Sihanouk, not to abdicate, saying he is the only person capable of unifying the country's various factions.

Sihanouk has said he is unhappy on the throne and was considering abdicating following what he described as mounting attacks on the royal family and his achievements as national leader during the 1950s and 1960s.

The 74-year-old monarch, in a written interview conducted by his cabinet and released by the palace on Wednesday, pledged that he would never take part in general elections due next year or form a party.

"It is up to him to decide. I hope that he will not (abdicate) -- on the contrary, more than ever he is the cement of the Cambodians and the only one who could really unify all the Cambodians," Ranariddh told reporters after launching an alliance of his royalist FUNCINPEC party and three other parties.

"I hope for the sake of the country he will not. The king should listen only to the people of Cambodia," the prince said, adding that the political programme of the National United Front stressed Sihanouk's vital importance as a unifying figure.
Sihanouk flew to China on Wednesday for an eye operation and a medical check-up.
He left at a time of heightened tension between FUNCINPEC and the Cambodian People's Party (CPP), which formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
Some analysts believe the CPP and its leader, co-Premier Hun Sen, fear the king might step down to lead a royalist party to victory at the polls on the back of his grass roots popularity.
Sihanouk said in the interview that the problem he faced in abdicating was that he would likely be blamed for anything bad that befell Cambodia be or accused of wanting to get involved in politics.
He said he had declared he would not to step down before 2000 to reassure those who feared he would run in the 1998 elections.
